title: SDK error ergonomics: user-facing wrappers, diagnostic IDs, and language-specific examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Standardize the public SDK error surface across Python/TypeScript/Go with: (1) concise user-facing wrappers that include actionable remediation hints, (2) stable diagnostic IDs suitable for support and telemetry, and (3) idiomatic language examples and migration notes. Goal is to reduce developer confusion, improve observability of customer issues, and enable deterministic retry behaviors for recoverable errors.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs expose a consistent high-level Error type with: error_code, diagnostic_id, user_message, is_retriable
Diagnostic IDs are stable strings (e.g., RX-SDK-<4hex>) and appear in logs/telemetry and error messages
Docs include language-specific code examples for catching and handling errors for sync/async and streaming flows
A migration guide and codemod examples exist for existing consumers to adopt the new surface
E2E tests validate mapping between runtime errors (gRPC/HTTP) and SDK error codes, including backoff/retry hints
proposed_solution: Introduce a small, backwards-compatible wrapper layer in each SDK that maps transport and runtime errors to a canonical SDKError. The wrapper will attach a stable diagnostic_id and expose a human-friendly user_message and machine-friendly error_code. For streaming endpoints, provide a StreamError variant with resume_hint. Implementation will be incremental: 1) mapping library + tests, 2) public API surface + docs, 3) codemods and sample migrations.
migration_plan: Ship the wrapper as opt-in behind a minor version flag in Python and TS; default enable in Go once validated
Publish migration guide and sample codemods: replace catch blocks that inspect raw HTTP/gRPC errors with SDKError checks
Run a 2-week dogfood on internal Redwood services and instrument occurrences via diagnostics pipeline
Follow-up patch to mark old raw-error helpers deprecated and schedule removal in next major
notes: Trade-offs: adding a wrapper adds a small allocation and additional call frames on hot paths; benchmarking of common sync/async flows required
We prefer stable diagnostic IDs over transient numeric codes to make customer support easier across SDK versions
Avoid exposing internal transport details (stack traces, raw gRPC codes) in default user_message to reduce support noise; surface them in telemetry only
Ensure error_code values are descriptive (e.g., RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, KV_CACHE_MISS, MODEL_NOT_LOADED) to make automated routing easier
